Automated content and build controls help enforce approved copy, structural
requirements, placeholder handling, and selected prohibited phrases. They do

---

`landing-manifest.json` declares **67** events and the code fires
exactly that set — `_build/audit-integrity.js` fails if they diverge.

## Restricted data — what is never sent

No event payload carries a name, email, phone number, free-text city or
state, narrative text, account data, property data, or any other personal or
financial information. Event payloads are built from element attributes and
fixed enumerated values only; element text is never used as a label.

The visitor’s self-reported `discovery_source` is stored separately from
tracked attribution (`utm_*`, `referrer`, `first_touch_source`,
`last_touch_source`) and is never overwritten by it.

## Payload fields in use

```text
campaign_theme                cta_location                  error_category
expanded_state                faq_id                        faq_index
filter                        form_step                     internal_destination
landing_page                  lead_status                   ltv_band
market                        market_page                   mi_applies
months_saved                  page_id                       page_path
page_type                     program_interest              source_page
term_years                    timeline                      transaction_goal
view
```

## Super Jumbo event mapping (§3)

§3: “Avoid double-counting page views and form events. Use shared page/form
events with page-level properties where the suite already does so, rather than
firing redundant page-specific duplicates.”

The DFW Super Jumbo page therefore fires **no page-specific duplicates**. It
carries page-level properties on the shared events instead:

```text
page_type    = super_jumbo          <body data-page-type>
market       = dallas_fort_worth    <body data-market-page>
cta_location = hero | qualifying_paths | related_options | form
```

Both page-level properties ride along on every `data-track` event from
`analytics.js`, so no per-CTA wiring can omit them.

### Replacement events for the names not emitted

| Handoff event name | Replacement event | Trigger | Required properties |
|---|---|---|---|
| `super_jumbo_page_view` | `view_super_jumbo_page` | page view | `page_type`, `market` |
| `super_jumbo_form_start` | `hero_form_start` | first interaction with the scenario-review form | `page_type`, `market`, `form_step` |
| `super_jumbo_form_submit` | `scenario_form_submit` | form submitted | `page_type`, `market` |
| `super_jumbo_qualifying_paths_click` | `internal_path_click` | click on a Potential Qualifying Paths card link | `page_type`, `market`, `cta_location=qualifying_paths`, `internal_destination` |
| `super_jumbo_primary_cta_click` | `closing_cta_click` | click on the closing CTA to the scenario-review form | `page_type`, `market`, `cta_location=form` |

`cta_location=hero` is defined but never emitted on this page. The
scenario-review form sits inside the hero, and §2.2 approved not adding a
hero CTA that jumps to a form already visible in the hero, so there is no
hero CTA to attribute. Recorded here rather than emitted with no trigger.

Status: **Owner-approved** (§3). **Launch dependency** — §5.2 requires GA4
configuration, dashboards, reports and downstream consumers to be updated
for these names before production.
